description:
FILED s464 (Fable, 2026-09-02) while answering the USER's question "are there optimizations left in the areas where PCL already beats perl?".  docs/faster-codegen-suggestions.md section 5 measured two array wins that no task ever carried: A3 `push @a, X` on a never-referenced, non-escaping `my @a` -> `(vector-push-extend X v)` instead of p-push-impl (arg flattening + box handling per call; ~7x at 2M pushes) -- the arrhash profile (s464) still shows p-push-impl at 12 % total with %p-array-store-scalar under it; A5 recognise the classic comparators (`{ $a <=> $b }`, `{ $b <=> $a }`, `{ $a cmp $b }`, `{ $a->{k} <=> $b->{k} }`, Schwartzian forms) and emit `(sort v #'<)` / `#'string<` on unboxed keys instead of a per-comparison generic funcall through boxes (~6x at 50 elems x 100k).  A5 has no bench row yet: add one (`sort { $a <=> $b } @nums` over 50 elements x N) before measuring, the way #881/#981 added strcat/listcopy.  Both are Kind-A emissions (facts-licensed: the array's escape/reference facts from VarAnnotator; the comparator SHAPE for A5) and both must run identically under PCL_OPT=none.  VERIFY FIRST that neither shipped under another name (grep Pl/Passes.pm and the runtime for a sort fast path / vector-push-extend emission); if one did, close this half with the pointer.  BAR per item: bench row before/after with a control pair; full sweep; companion op/sort.t + op/push.t; guards incl. the NEGATIVE cases (a comparator reading anything but $a/$b; `sort` with a named sub; an array that is referenced / passed whole / captured must keep p-push-impl).

== s469bh (Opus, 2026-09-05): BOTH HALVES VERIFIED UNSHIPPED, SIZED, AND DESIGNED; NEITHER SHIPPED ==

VERIFICATION FIRST, as the task asks.  Neither half has shipped under another
name: `Pl/Passes.pm`'s %KIND_A has no push or sort entry; the only
`vector-push-extend` under `Pl/` is ExprToCL's list-building, not a push
emission; the only `stable-sort` in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp` is `p-sort`'s own
generic comparator loop.  `push @a, $i*2` on a `my @a` still emits
`(p-push @a (p-* $i 2))`; `sort { $a <=> $b } @src` still emits
`(p-sort (p-sort-cmp ($a $b) (p-scalar-ctx (p-<=> $a $b))) @src)`.

THREE BENCH ROWS ADDED (they had to exist before either half could be
measured, the way #881/#981 added strcat/listcopy): `pushloc` (2M appends to a
never-referenced local array â arrhash-k pushes too, but under a hash
increment that dominates it), `sortnum` and `sortstr` (50 elements sorted 20k
times, ~5.6M comparisons each).

MEASURED CEILINGS.  Each is the SAME transpiled program with ONE form
replaced by hand (`scratch/s469bh/p996/*-A.lisp` vs `*-B.lisp`, timed against
ONE core, four series interleaved, best-of-K, by `scratch/s469bh/p996/ab-lisp.pl`
â the emission A/B methodology of tools/bench-emission-ab.pl applied to a form
that has no compiler yet).  See the s469bh report for the numbers and their
control spread.

=== A3 â `push @local, SCALAR` ===

THE SIZING CHANGED SINCE THE ~7x CATALOGUE NUMBER, and that matters: the
runtime under `p-push-impl` has been rewritten twice since s3xx.
`%p-array-store-scalar` already takes a RAW element (`%p-storable-raw`,
boxed-aggregates s455) and `%p-vpush` already has the simple-vector
capacity fast path that #811/s458ak added.  What is left between
`(p-push @a X)` and the ideal is: the `p-push` macro's per-call
`(unless (boundp '@a) â¦)`, `p-push-impl`'s `&rest` list consing, its
array-shape type test, and its four-way per-item cond (flatten marker / raw
vector / raw hash / scalar).

THE BLOCKER IS NOT THE EMISSION, IT IS THE FACTS.  `Pl::VarAnnotator` is
SCALAR-ONLY by construction: `_analyze_tree`'s decl walk does
`next unless $var =~ /^\$\w+$/`, and the verdict loop runs over
`keys %{$ctx->{decl_count}}`, so no `@name` ever gets a verdict.  A3's
licence â never referenced (`\@a`), never passed whole, never captured by a
closure, never aliased by `foreach`, never `local`ised, never tied or blessed
through a reference, not `@_` â is a NEW fact family over array names, plus a
consumer key, plus the threading into Parser2.  That is the item; the
emission itself is a few lines.  Do NOT shape-test at the push site: the
whole point of the registry is that the licence is a proven fact, and an
array that escapes ANYWHERE in the region must keep `p-push-impl`.

The emission, once the facts exist: a Kind-A name `local-push` in
`Pl/Passes.pm`, and `(%p-push1 @a X)` where

    (declaim (inline %p-push1))
    (defun %p-push1 (arr item)
      (%p-array-store-scalar arr item)      ; COPY semantics + raw-element rules
      (length arr))                          ; push's value is the new length

`%p-array-store-scalar` is deliberately the SAME function `p-push-impl`
calls, so copy semantics, the blessed/dualvar/ref-container rules and the
raw-element gate cannot drift.  It is licensed ONLY for a single SCALAR
argument: `push @a, @b` / `%h` / a list-valued call must keep the generic
path, because the flattening is what the four-way cond is for and that is a
separate licence.

=== A5 â the four classic comparators ===

THE COST IS NOT WHERE THE CATALOGUE SAID, and this is the finding.  Per
comparison the generic path pays: TWO `make-p-box` allocations (p-sort boxes
each raw element before handing the pair to the block, so \$a/\$b alias
stably â [perl #78194]), a `catch :p-return` frame (p-sort-cmp wraps every
comparator body), a dynamic bind of the package `$a`/`$b`, a `p-scalar-ctx`
bind, an out-of-line `funcall`, and a `to-number` of the comparator's result.

AND BEFORE ANY OF THAT: `%p-collect-list` â which p-sort calls to collect its
list â PROMOTES every raw element of the source array to a box in place
(`%p-elem-cell`).  Promotion is MONOTONE, so a plain `sort { $a <=> $b } @a`
makes `@a` pay box indirection on every later read FOREVER.  That is a cost
the row `sortnum` shares with `feread`'s ARM-A story and it is invisible in
the sort's own time.

The four plain shapes â `{ $a <=> $b }`, `{ $b <=> $a }`, `{ $a cmp $b }`,
`{ $b cmp $a }`, where the block references exactly the current package's
`$a`/`$b` and nothing else â never take a reference to either, so nothing
needs promoting and nothing needs boxing.  Emission: a Kind-A name
`classic-sort` and `(%p-sort-num-asc @a)` / `-desc` / `%p-sort-str-asc` /
`-desc`, over a collector that copies raw slots instead of promoting them.

CORRECTNESS NOTES THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST HONOUR (each already checked
against the runtime):
  * STABILITY: `stable-sort`, never `sort` â p-sort is stable today and perl's
    mergesort is stable in practice; a change here would be observable.
  * NUMIFICATION must be the generic path's: `p-<=>` numifies through
    `to-number` ("10abc" -> 10, undef -> 0, a ref -> its address).  `:key
    #'to-number` is that same reading.
  * `cmp` compares codepoints and `p-str-cmp`'s fast path IS CL `string<` on
    two strings, so `#'string< :key #'to-string` matches it exactly â but only
    on the fast path: `%p-str-cmp-slow` owns overload and tie.
  * AN OBJECT OR A TIED ELEMENT MUST NOT TAKE THE FAST PATH (an overloaded
    `<=>`/`""`/`0+` handler and a tie FETCH are both observable per
    comparison).  The cheap program-level answer already exists and is the
    idiom `%compound-arith-form` uses: `*p-any-overload-registered*` is NIL in
    any program that never says `use overload`.  A tie proxy needs a
    per-element test in the collector, which is where the elements are
    already being walked.
  * NaN: the generic path answers `(< (to-number (p-<=> a b)) 0)`, and
    `p-<=>` on a NaN gives undef -> 0 -> "not less".  A bare `#'<` on a NaN
    float does not agree.  Probe it before shipping.

KEY-EXTRACTOR SHAPES (`$a->{k} <=> $b->{k}`, the Schwartzian transform) ARE
NOT LICENSED and were not measured as if they were: an element read is
observable per comparison (a tie FETCH, an overloaded `""` on the key), so a
decorate-once transform changes how many times the program looks at the data.
They stay on the generic path.

=== THE NUMBERS (quiet box, 2026-09-05) ===

Standing rows, best-of-5, two runs (pcl-column run-to-run spread <= 2.9 %):

  bench       perl(s)   pcl(s)  pcl/perl      run 2
  pushloc      0.1101   0.0532     0.48x      0.1072 / 0.0528  0.49x
  sortnum      0.0252   0.1843     7.31x      0.0261 / 0.1897  7.26x
  sortstr      0.0678   0.2446     3.61x      0.0694 / 0.2377  3.42x

Ceilings (one form of the transpiled program replaced by hand; one core, four
series interleaved, best-of-7).  Byte-identical CONTROL pairs in the same
window read +1.1 % (sortnum) and -2.2 % (pushloc):

  sortnum-ceiling  A 0.1845  B 0.0953   -48.4 %
  sortstr-ceiling  A 0.2490  B 0.1484   -40.4 %
  pushloc-ceiling  A 0.0557  B 0.0329   -40.9 %

=== THE PRIORITY IS THE OTHER WAY ROUND ===

`push` on a local array is ALREADY 2x FASTER than perl.  The catalogue's ~7x
was measured at s3xx, before raw elements (s455) and %p-vpush's simple-vector
fast path (#811, s458ak) collected most of it; A3 would take the row from
0.48x to about 0.29x.  Real, but a filler.

`sort` with the commonest comparator in Perl is **7.3x SLOWER than perl** --
the worst ratio on this board apart from the pack oracle -- and the NAIVE
ceiling already halves it.  That ceiling is a FLOOR on A5's prize, not the
whole of it: it still goes through %p-collect-list and its monotone
promotion.  A5 is the Target-A item; A3 is the smaller one AND the bigger
job (the facts family).  Whoever takes #996 next should take A5 first.

=== A5 SHIPPED (s470a5, Opus, 2026-09-05) â A3 IS STILL OPEN ===

`sort LIST' and the four classic comparator blocks now lower to
(%p-sort-classic MODE ARGS...).  Two files: Pl/ClassicSort.pm (the pass) and
one block in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp.  Guard Pl/t/classic-sort-01.t (27 rows,
5.1 s).  Generation v2-700.

THE NUMBERS (tools/bench-exec.pl, best-of-5, three interleaved passes;
A = PCL_OPT=-classic-sort = today's general form, B = the pass on; box shared
with a sibling agent, load 1.5-2.5):

  row      A pcl(s) x3               B pcl(s) x3               best A -> best B     ratio
  sortnum  0.1854 0.1862 0.1963      0.0842 0.0846 0.0841      -54.6 %              7.39x -> 3.15x
  sortstr  0.2432 0.2617 0.2549      0.1312 0.1305 0.1301      -46.5 %              3.53x -> 1.87x

Both BEAT the hand-replaced ceilings this task measured (-48.4 % / -40.4 %) --
the difference is the non-promoting collector, which the ceiling probe could
not include.  Controls all inside their own spread: cfor, arrhash, arrhash-k,
feread (feread's own five-run spread with an IDENTICAL setting is 7.3 %, and
its emission is byte-identical on both sides).

THE CORPUS CENSUS (250 sort calls over lib/**.pm + cpan-tests/modules/** +
perl-tests/*.t): 149 are a licensed SHAPE (60 %) and 110 of those also carry a
licence (44 % of every sort in the corpus).  The 39 licensed shapes with no
licence are almost all an `after-comma' argument position with an @array
source.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE DESIGN, BOTH MEASURED:
  1. `values' IS NOT A FRESH SOURCE.  `for my $v (sort { $a <=> $b } values
     %h) { $v .= "!" }' writes back into the hash, in perl AND in PCL.  So do
     `grep' and a nested `sort'.  A USER SUB CALL is fresh even when the sub
     returns @arr or `values %h' -- the call boundary copies (probed).
  2. FIVE modes, not four.  :default (`sort LIST') is separate from :str-asc
     (`{ $a cmp $b }') because their FALLBACKS differ: p-sort's no-comparator
     arm stringifies while the block dispatches a `cmp' OVERLOAD.  A guard row
     proves it with a class whose cmp handler reverses the order.

A DEVIATION FOR REVIEW: `classic-sort' is a Kind-B CLForm pass, not a Kind-A
emission site.  The licence is a fact about the sort's CONSUMER and the
consumers are six different emitters, while the PExpr tree has no parent link
-- a Kind-A gate would have to be spelled at all six (rule 11's hard stop).
The lowered CLForm tree is the one place they all pass through
(Parser2::_lower_program: "the one place a lowered tree becomes text") and it
already carries the `p-foreach-raw' head, i.e. VarAnnotator's read-only
verdict, so the pass CONSULTS that fact rather than computing a second one.
PCL_OPT=none and PCL_OPT=-classic-sort restore today's emission either way.

BARS: gate 200 files / 6820 rows, only the 13 known pclxs xs rows failing;
PCL_OPT=none corpus-diff vs ccdb6b7 IDENTICAL over 111 files + 6 shapes (the
proof that the pass is the only emission change); with it on, 12 corpus files
/ 90 regions and 66 wide-population files / 152 hunks, every one of them
(p-sort ...) -> (%p-sort-classic ...), RCDIFF 0 over 1007 files; companion
op/sort.t C 183/22 before, after and under PCL_OPT=none, 0 NEW ROW.

FILED: #1125 -- emission is NONDETERMINISTIC (a Perl arrayref address in the
:captures slot), pre-existing, found by this session's byte-compares.

A3 (`push @local, X' -> %p-push1) is UNTOUCHED and remains this task's open
half; the sizing note above still stands (it needs a new array-fact family in
VarAnnotator, which is scalar-only by construction).

=== A5's MERGE REVIEW (s470a5, Fable) â RULINGS AND THE A3 PREREQUISITE ===

APPROVED.  The Kind-B deviation is RATIFIED: the licence is a fact about the
consumer, and the lowered tree is the one place the six consumers pass through
(rule 11).  The `values'-is-not-fresh correction is confirmed and adopted.

Review probes added three facts, all now in Pl/ClassicSort.pm's header, the
ir-spec section and Pl/t/classic-sort-01.t:
  * a `do { â¦ }' TAIL IS NOT a copying consumer -- perl hands its aliases
    through (`$_++ for do { sort @d }' writes back), and the pass correctly
    leaves it generic (guard row);
  * `eval { }' and a SUB TAIL do copy (the sub tail is licensed, guard row);
  * `sort @objs' with an overloaded `cmp' is perl `c b a' and PCL `a b c' in
    BOTH modes -- the PRE-EXISTING #1021, not A5's; the :default fallback goes
    through p-sort, so #1021's fix carries automatically (the runtime docstring
    now says so instead of claiming the no-block arm "stringifies").

**A3 IS BLOCKED ON #1140** (filed at this review): the VarAnnotator ARRAY-fact
family (never-written-in-region / non-escaping `@name').  A3's licence IS that
fact family, and the same missing facts are why `foreach-raw' -- and therefore
classic-sort's foreach consumer licence, which consults foreach-raw's verdict
by design -- does not see a write to the ARRAY by another path during the
loop.  Both reproducers, perl-vs-PCL verbatim, are in #1140.  A5's foreach
licence STAYS: it is exactly as sound as foreach-raw itself, no better and no
worse.


=== A3 SHIPPED (s470bj, Opus, 2026-09-05) â #996 IS NOW CLOSED (both halves) ===

`push @a, SCALAR` on a non-escaping `my @a` emits `(%p-push1 @a X)`.  Kind-A
name `local-push` in Pl/Passes.pm; the licence is #1140's array-fact family,
which shipped in the same commit (d54b798, generation v2-720).

    (declaim (inline %p-push1))
    (defun %p-push1 (arr item)
      (%p-array-store-scalar arr item)
      (length arr))

`%p-array-store-scalar` is DELIBERATELY the same function p-push-impl calls
for a scalar item, so the copy semantics, the blessed/dualvar/is-ref rules and
the raw-element gate cannot drift between the two paths.  What is skipped is
everything p-push-impl needs only because its arguments are unknown: the
p-push macro's per-call `(boundp '@a)` auto-declare, the `&rest` list consing,
the array-shape type test (`%p-push-cold`) and the four-way per-item cond.

TWO HALVES, AND ONLY THE FIRST IS A FACT, exactly as this task demanded:
  * THE ARRAY â a `my @a` declared in the emitting region with `escapes` = 0
    AND an emitted symbol that is a let-bound lexical (a package cell is a
    different container, and it is the one case where the macro's auto-declare
    has work to do).  No shape test at the push site.
  * THE ITEM â `_push_item_is_scalar`, a property of the argument alone:
    literals and `$`-sigiled leaves (via `_node_is_definitely_scalar`), a
    binary arith/string/comparison operator, an interpolated string, an
    anon array/hash/sub constructor, one element access (4 spellings), a
    unary `! - + ~`, `++`/`--`, and `\` over ONE named container.
    `push @a, @b` / `%h` / `keys` / `(1,2)` / two arguments / a user sub call
    / `@$r` all keep p-push-impl.

A READ-ONLY ARRAY CANNOT REACH IT: `Internals::SvREADONLY(@a, 1)` passes the
array to a call, which is one of #1140's escape spellings (probed).  And if
the licence were ever wrong the failure is LOUD, not silent (rule 12):
`%p-vpush` finds no fill pointer and VECTOR-PUSH-EXTEND signals.

THE NUMBERS (tools/bench-exec.pl, best-of-5, THREE A/B rounds of the same
tree; A = PCL_OPT=-local-push = today's emission.  The box was shared with two
sibling agents â round 1 ran at load 8.7 and its perl column reads 0.157 s
against 0.109 s in round 3 â so read the RATIOS and the per-round deltas):

  row         A pcl(s)              B pcl(s)              delta                 ratio
  pushloc     0.0786 0.0563 0.0539  0.0450 0.0319 0.0305  -42.7/-43.3/-43.4 %   0.48x -> 0.28x
  arrhash-k   0.1097 0.0779 0.0717  0.0988 0.0687 0.0644  -9.9/-11.8/-10.2 %    1.15x -> 1.03x
  cfor (ctl)  0.0476 0.0320 0.0309  0.0487 0.0335 0.0313  +2.3/+4.7/+1.3 %      unmoved

pushloc lands exactly on the ceiling this task measured by hand (-40.9 %).
`feread`/`feread2` do NOT move (0.44x/0.45x against the 0.47x #862 recorded)
and both keep `p-foreach-raw` in the emission.

COVERAGE, measured: `local-push` fires 3x over lib/**.pm (Cwd, List::Util
twice) and 3x over perl-tests/*.t, with 23 lib and 127 corpus push sites
keeping the general path â test files are eval-heavy and `escapes` is a REGION
fact, so one string eval revokes every array in a file.  Over the wide
population (perl 5.40.3 t/ + cpan-tests) it fires in ~30 files.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: `_node_is_definitely_scalar` was not widened,
although the item licence is that predicate one notch wider.  Its other
consumer (gen_progn_form's `vector` vs `p-flatten-args`) would change emission
corpus-wide â a separate optimization, filed as #1141 with a bench row as its
first step.
subject: Perf: catalogue items never taken -- A3 `push @local, X` on a non-escaping local array -> vector-push-extend (~7x measured s3xx), A5 classic sort comparators `{ $a <=> $b }` / `{ $a cmp $b }` / key extractors -> native sort on unboxed keys (~6x): both still spell the generic path (verify before starting)
